title: Keyframe design and animation composition
learningObjectives: Explain keyframe design and animation composition and create motion that respects user preferences.

understand.concept: Keyframe animations define intermediate states using percentages or from/to. Multiple animations can be composed by listing animation names and matching comma-separated timing values. Animation composition can include delays, directions, fill modes, and play states.
understand.whyItMatters: Clear keyframe design keeps motion understandable and maintainable. Avoid animating many properties without purpose, and ensure the content remains available when animation is disabled.
understand.analogy: Keyframes are checkpoints in a motion sequence; composition combines several small movements into one coordinated result.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual animation, rendering, and preference handling follow CSS and browser behaviour.

explain.narrative: The badge uses an entrance animation and a separate glow animation. Each animation has its own timing entry.

examples.explanation: The badge uses an entrance animation and a separate glow animation. Each animation has its own timing entry.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered example showing the animation or user-preference behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create two keyframe animations and apply them together. Keep the movement subtle and add a reduced-motion fallback.
practise.independentTask: Build a small motion-enhanced component. Provide a static or reduced-motion state and test the result with keyboard interaction.
hints: Keep essential content visible without animation.
Test light/dark and forced-colours preferences where relevant.
Measure performance on a representative device.
